newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, no election fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down, no election fears.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 185 basis points at 19.90 percent amid market confidence over the outlook for international interest rates and approaching mid-term elections in Mexico.
"The secondary market is giving a vote of confidence in last night's fall in primary rates. What's more, speculation has eased off and secondary rates were too high," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.95 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 95 basis points since last week.

Fixed-income analysts said secondary rates had fallen in part due to accurate market forecasts that the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee would announce no changes in U.S. interest rates during the day.
"It confirmed news that had been expected, but was nonetheless important," one analyst said.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity by draining a total of 3.994 billion pesos through three direct Cetes sales and six repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile ended down 190 basis points at 21.50 percent.
Liquidity of 1.168 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
